rule.description: A repository-declared named interface unifies capability methods from unrelated roles; capability methods that are never invoked through the interface force every implementor to provide them (via fabricated carrier stubs) and force every consumer bound to the interface to depend on capabilities it never uses.

checks.description: A capability method declared on a repository-declared named interface is never invoked on any operand statically typed as that interface; the method is pure surface forced onto every implementor and every interface-bound consumer.
checks.detected_relation: declared named interface -> capability method never selected through the interface
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The interface exceeds the dependency boundary of its consumers: the serialized-invoke, streaming, context, content-typing, lifecycle, and HTTP key/value transport roles are merged into unified capability surfaces, so implementors must provide unused capabilities and consumers of these interfaces must depend on capabilities they never use.

matches.evidence: The unified Handler interface declares ContentType func()(string) among 5 capability methods; non-test declarations never invoke ContentType on a Handler-typed operand (response typing runs through a separate anonymous-interface probe of handler return values), yet every implementor must provide it and every interface-bound consumer (doRuntimeAPILoop, handleInvoke, Function) transitively depends on it.

The unified Handler interface declares Close func() error although response cleanup runs through the separate response-probing pipeline (io.Closer) that never held a Handler value; the only implementation is a no-op stub on handlerFunc, and no non-test declaration invokes Close through Handler.

The named lambda.httpClient transport interface requires Get(url string)(*http.Response, error), but the repository builds every request with http.NewRequest and executes it with Do; neither runtimeAPIClient nor extensionAPIClient ever selects Get on the interface type, and the only implementor is the standard library *http.Client.

The named lambda.httpClient transport interface requires Post(url, contentType string, body io.Reader)(*http.Response, error) although both consumers construct requests explicitly (Headers and request bodies must be set up per call); no non-test declaration selects Post on this interface type.

The callback response transport interface grew from its single-method form to require Get, but sendWith only performs a signed PUT via http.NewRequest/Do; no non-test declaration in the repository selects Get on this interface.

The callback response transport interface requires Post although the only consumer, sendWith, does not even set a Content-Type (req.Header.Del) and performs a PUT; no non-test declaration selects Post on this interface.

checks.description: A concrete method exists only to satisfy a capability of a fat repository-declared named interface that is never invoked through it, and the concrete method has no non-test invocation anywhere in the repository.
checks.detected_relation: concrete carrier stub -> never-invoked interface capability
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Implementors are forced to fabricate capability stubs whose only purpose is to satisfy the unified interface; the stubs are reachable only through the interface dispatch chain that by construction chooses the capability zero times, so they are dead weight forced onto the implementing types.

matches.evidence: handlerFunc.ContentType is a fabricated stub returning the constant contentTypeJSON regardless of what the wrapped handler function produced; it exists only so the function adapter satisfies the unified Handler interface, and the repository contains zero non-test invocations of it.

handlerFunc.Close is a fabricated no-op stub (return nil) attached only to satisfy the unified Handler interface; the runtime never closes handlers, and zero non-test declarations invoke it (resource cleanup runs through the independent response-probing pipeline), so it is never executed.

excluded.reason: Live contrast, not a forced stub: these concrete methods on the pooled response type are invoked through direct selection and through the response-probing pipeline (anonymous interface probe in invoke_loop.go, io.Closer). The rule deliberately does not credit dispatch through anonymous or standard-library-declared interfaces, but these methods are invoked directly on their concrete type, so they are outside the report set by construction, not by oversight.

Single-capability private assertion seam (Invoke only) that keeps pre-existing Invoke-only Handler implementations usable while the public interface is widened; its single method is invoked through the interface, so the rule intentionally reports nothing on it. An interface with one capability cannot force an unneeded dependency.

Test-file positions are intentionally outside rule scope: the rule measures production dependency boundaries and must stay robust against test scaffolding; the same-named stubs added to this test double mirror, but do not participate in, the repository's coupling.
Test double outside production scope; the stubs exist only to let the fake satisfy the widened interface inside exercised tests.

excluded.structure: implicit implementor of both httpClient interfaces
excluded.reason: The only implementor of the widened transport interfaces; standard-library types are outside repository rule scope, but this exclusion is recorded because it explains why the transport findings report no in-package concrete carrier.
